# Storyfolio

Makes one kind of portfolio site: one long scroll that introduces the person in 3D, each chapter's scene a picture of what it is about.

Start from the recorded handover on a continuation. For a requested build, sketch concepts at stop 2; build the chosen site after storyboard approval. A planning-only request still ends at the storyboard.

## Stops

Between stops you work by yourself. At each stop the person decides one thing. You go on only when their answer is in the conversation and you have written it into the file.

| Stop | First open | You put to the person | You go on when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Read | `references/reading-a-profile.md` | What you found, as facts to confirm and questions to answer. No concept or design | They have answered, and `docs/story/facts.md` holds their answers |
| 2. Concept | `references/concept.md` | Three concepts, runnable for a requested build, and which you would choose | They have picked one, or told you to pick, and `docs/story/concepts.md` says which |
| 3. Storyboard | `references/storyboard.md` | The script of the whole page | They have said yes to it |
| 4. Spine | `references/building.md`, `engine/README.md` | A runnable opening, middle and ending in two or three looks | They have chosen a look |
| 5. Chapters | `references/building.md` | The remaining chapters and three whole-beat wording versions | They have chosen the wording |
| 6. Finish | `engine/README.md` | The checked site and what still needs their review | Their actual review is recorded |

**When starting from profile material, your first reply is the first stop, and no more than that.** Brief build-setup notes do not advance the design. People ask for the whole plan at once: the idea, the scroll, the colours. Do not give it yet, and say why in a sentence. A plan made now is made from your reading of a resume, and a resume leaves out exactly what a site must not get wrong: whose result a number was, what a title hides, who took a photograph. Once they have answered you will have a better idea, and it will not have to be taken apart.

## Ask or decide

Ask the person when a thing is:

1. a fact only they know,
2. a claim that could embarrass them if it were wrong,
3. taste on what a visitor sees first: the concept, the look, the opening words,
4. anything that publishes, costs money, or shows another person or an employer's work.

Everything else you decide. Write each decision into `docs/story/decided-for-you.md`: what you decided, why, and how to change it.

If the person will not answer, or tells you to decide everything, open `references/asking.md`.

## What you keep

In the person's own folder, so that a later session can go on from the files alone:

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `docs/story/facts.md` | The fact sheet, each fact with where it came from, and the person's answers |
| `docs/story/concepts.md` | The three concepts, which was picked, and why |
| `docs/story/storyboard.md` | The script |
| `docs/story/decided-for-you.md` | What you decided without asking |
| `docs/story/handover.md` | What exists, what the person has said, what is next |

## What holds from the first stop on

- **Nothing about the person is invented.** You know that a number, an employer, a title and a quote are facts. So is every small thing a sentence says on its way: what was wrong before they came, how often a thing is used, which came first, why, how a thing was left, what it taught them. That sounds like writing, and it is a claim. Before handing over any reply or file, check each claim against the fact sheet, including introductory summaries, working titles and words in the scene. Read the supporting line and its unresolved questions, not just its reference. It must establish the whole claim: a topic attached to one item does not establish the topic of another. Wording that depends on an unanswered question stays out of the introduction and the planned page, even if copied from a profile. Remove it or list it as a question to confirm. An illustration of the kind of thing they work with, labelled as one, claims nothing: a plated dessert, a status page. A particular design, a measured value or an event does. An empty scene is no safer.
- **A number is used as the person confirmed it,** with what it measures and whose result it is.
- **What is someone else's is asked about before it is planned for:** a photograph a photographer took, a friend's drawing, a quote, an employer's screens, a story with a patient or a client in it.
# Storyfolio engine

A starting project for one scroll and one story in 3D: shared pieces for what carries on
through the story, and a scene of its own for each chapter.
The supplied page is a placeholder that tests the engine: one sheet whose
picture changes by chapter. It has no design in it; replace all of `content/`.

Taken from V3 at `163b8ceb302b7b4e5beeff8f1161f4cdc7663b15` and made
independent of that site's content, paper shapes and assets. The source
project is unchanged. Storyfolio's engine and generated SVGs are MIT licensed.

## Start

Use Node 22.18 or later with native TypeScript support. Scaffold this folder
with `node <installed-skill>/scripts/scaffold.mjs <site-folder>`. Existing
`docs/story/` files are kept; any conflicting engine path aborts the copy.
Then, in the new site folder:

```bash
npm ci
npm run browsers
npm run dev
```

Open the local address printed by Next.js. Append `?look=dark` to choose a
look and `?fps` to show the frame meter. The appearance switch preserves
other query parameters, the fragment and the current scroll position.
Read the frame meter on a real phone; software rendering in a headless
browser does not measure phone performance.

Never install dependencies inside an installed skill. The copied project
belongs to the person, has its own lockfile, and does not depend on the
skill after scaffolding. System fonts make builds independent of remote
font services. Add licensed local files with `next/font/local` if needed;
the scene starts without waiting for them and redraws faces when fonts load.

## From storyboard to content

`lib/story/` contains pure, tested calculations. `components/story/` owns
the browser and scene. The person's story belongs in `content/`:

| File | Storyboard input |
|---|---|
| `story.ts` | Chapter IDs, names, roles, beat IDs and screen heights; one fixed piece count |
| `formations.ts` | A rest formation for every beat; optional `within` formation reached as its rest is scrolled |
| `faces.ts` | Pictures or canvas drawing functions for a beat and piece |
| `copy.ts` | Metadata, language, labels and complete HTML text |
| `looks.ts` | Ground, text and surface colors, lights and matte/no floor |
| `extras.ts` | Each chapter's own scene: lazy imports, each in its own error boundary |
| `links.ts` | Ordinary HTML links over a named piece at a named beat |
| `checks.json` | Optional checks of capabilities this fixture exercises |

Use `as const satisfies StoryDef` for the story and
`satisfies Record<BeatId, BeatFormation>` for formations. `checkStory`
also rejects invalid IDs, heights, piece counts and face references at
runtime. A formation contains one position, rotation and size per piece,
plus framing. `layouts.ts` supplies stack, fan, ring, grid, row and seeded
scatter; `measure` bounds their rotated faces. Depth, a custom shape's
extent and a whole formation's turn can require extra framing room.

The HTML in `app/page.tsx` follows the same beat order using `Chapter` and
`Beat`. A `Beat` can carry a static `fallback` image or diagram. Keep one
`h1`, stable chapter heading IDs and every factual claim in HTML. The check
script verifies the rendered beat IDs against the content contract.

The bundle type is in `components/story/types.ts`. Import a bundle inside a
client component, as `content/experience.tsx` does, and pass server-rendered
HTML as children. Bundles contain drawing functions and component loaders,
so cannot be serialized across a server/client prop boundary.

A custom `Piece` component receives its index, face material and look.
Build it at unit width/height centered at the origin. Its parent group gets
the formation's position, rotation and width/height scale each frame. Keep
materials present from the first frame. Extras receive the shared frame,
look, reduced-motion flag and control store, and stay mounted from a beat
before their chapter to a beat after it. Drive each with
`chapterPresence(story, chapter, frameRef.current.beat)` from
`lib/story/story.ts`, 0 to 1 over the travel in and back to 0 over the travel
out: let it grow, unfold, fly in or turn into the next scene with that value,
so that one chapter's scene grows out of the last. Never switch one on or off
at a chapter's edge. Their shapes are children of the formation group.

Use `useExtraFrame` from `components/story/extra-frame.tsx` for an extra's
frame callback. It receives the same state, delta and optional XR frame as
React Three Fiber's `useFrame`. A synchronous exception disables that
callback immediately and unmounts its owning extra, leaving the core scene,
other extras and HTML running. Each extra also has a React boundary for
render failures and rejected lazy imports. For example:

```tsx
useExtraFrame(() => {
  const shown = chapterPresence(story, "middle", frameRef.current.beat);
  if (line.current) line.current.scale.x = Math.max(shown, 0.001);
});
```

`content/extras/middle-line.tsx` uses this hook. A raw third-party `useFrame`
callback, timer, event handler or rejected asynchronous task does not pass
through this guard. Handle failures at those boundaries explicitly;
wrapping a component in a React boundary does not catch them.

For caption controls, use `useControl` or `useControls` from
`components/story/controls.tsx` in a client component. Real controls remain
HTML. The canvas takes no pointer events. Overlay links are hidden and
removed from keyboard navigation outside their beat; supply the same
destination in the text for fallback access.

For a sketch, add a client component importing its own bundle and HTML to
`content/sketches/index.ts`. Its key becomes `/sketch/<id>`. The initial
registry is empty and unknown keys return 404.

## Check

```bash
npm test
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm run check
```

`check` builds, starts its own production server on a free local port,
runs the browser matrix and stops only that process group. It writes a
manifest, logs, reports and screenshots under `checks/<timestamp>/` and
returns a failure exit code for failed checks. `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`
selects an optional shared browser cache. `PLAYWRIGHT_CORE` is an optional
override; normally the installed local package provides the browser tool.

The matrix checks both looks at wide, short and phone sizes, reduced
motion, no WebGL and no JavaScript. Optional plain-story probes exercise
keyboard access and failed chapter loading. Context loss checks the HTML
fallback. Wide captures include the beginning, middle and end of each
beat's rest; reduced-motion captures also check that a stationary scene
stays still. Open every screenshot for overlap, clipping, legibility and
framing. Automatic passes do not replace visual review.

For a focused investigation use `npm run check -- --only=light-phone`.
`--skip-build` checks a previously built app and is diagnostic only.
Neither establishes a fresh full acceptance run. `scripts/shoot.mjs`
documents individual screenshots, blocked requests, look switching,
overflow and shader checks.

No JavaScript leaves the server-rendered text. No WebGL or a failed scene
leaves ordinary text and any beat's static image. Reduced motion cuts

---
name: storyfolio
description: Use when someone wants a personal portfolio site made from their profile, resume, LinkedIn or GitHub, especially one with 3D, scroll-driven animation or a story, or says their portfolio looks generic, templated or AI-made.
---

# Storyfolio

Makes one kind of portfolio site: one long scroll that introduces the person in 3D, each chapter's scene a picture of what it is about.

Start from the recorded handover on a continuation. For a requested build, sketch concepts at stop 2; build the chosen site after storyboard approval. A planning-only request still ends at the storyboard.

## Stops

Between stops you work by yourself. At each stop the person decides one thing. You go on only when their answer is in the conversation and you have written it into the file.

| Stop | First open | You put to the person | You go on when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Read | `references/reading-a-profile.md` | What you found, as facts to confirm and questions to answer. No concept or design | They have answered, and `docs/story/facts.md` holds their answers |
| 2. Concept | `references/concept.md` | Three concepts, runnable for a requested build, and which you would choose | They have picked one, or told you to pick, and `docs/story/concepts.md` says which |
| 3. Storyboard | `references/storyboard.md` | The script of the whole page | They have said yes to it |
| 4. Spine | `references/building.md`, `engine/README.md` | A runnable opening, middle and ending in two or three looks | They have chosen a look |
| 5. Chapters | `references/building.md` | The remaining chapters and three whole-beat wording versions | They have chosen the wording |
| 6. Finish | `engine/README.md` | The checked site and what still needs their review | Their actual review is recorded |

**When starting from profile material, your first reply is the first stop, and no more than that.** Brief build-setup notes do not advance the design. People ask for the whole plan at once: the idea, the scroll, the colours. Do not give it yet, and say why in a sentence. A plan made now is made from your reading of a resume, and a resume leaves out exactly what a site must not get wrong: whose result a number was, what a title hides, who took a photograph. Once they have answered you will have a better idea, and it will not have to be taken apart.

## Ask or decide

Ask the person when a thing is:

1. a fact only they know,
2. a claim that could embarrass them if it were wrong,
3. taste on what a visitor sees first: the concept, the look, the opening words,
4. anything that publishes, costs money, or shows another person or an employer's work.

Everything else you decide. Write each decision into `docs/story/decided-for-you.md`: what you decided, why, and how to change it.

If the person will not answer, or tells you to decide everything, open `references/asking.md`.

## What you keep

In the person's own folder, so that a later session can go on from the files alone:

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `docs/story/facts.md` | The fact sheet, each fact with where it came from, and the person's answers |
| `docs/story/concepts.md` | The three concepts, which was picked, and why |
| `docs/story/storyboard.md` | The script |
| `docs/story/decided-for-you.md` | What you decided without asking |
| `docs/story/handover.md` | What exists, what the person has said, what is next |

## What holds from the first stop on

- **Nothing about the person is invented.** You know that a number, an employer, a title and a quote are facts. So is every small thing a sentence says on its way: what was wrong before they came, how often a thing is used, which came first, why, how a thing was left, what it taught them. That sounds like writing, and it is a claim. Before handing over any reply or file, check each claim against the fact sheet, including introductory summaries, working titles and words in the scene. Read the supporting line and its unresolved questions, not just its reference. It must establish the whole claim: a topic attached to one item does not establish the topic of another. Wording that depends on an unanswered question stays out of the introduction and the planned page, even if copied from a profile. Remove it or list it as a question to confirm. An illustration of the kind of thing they work with, labelled as one, claims nothing: a plated dessert, a status page. A particular design, a measured value or an event does. An empty scene is no safer.
- **A number is used as the person confirmed it,** with what it measures and whose result it is.
- **What is someone else's is asked about before it is planned for:** a photograph a photographer took, a friend's drawing, a quote, an employer's screens, a story with a patient or a client in it.

#!/usr/bin/env node
/*
  Renders a page of the locally running site in headless Chromium, saves
  screenshots, and checks a few facts about it. A local tool for looking at
  visual work; nothing in the build depends on it.

  Install the engine's pinned development dependencies and Chromium with
  npm ci and npm run browsers. PLAYWRIGHT_CORE optionally overrides the
  engine's own playwright-core install:

    PLAYWRIGHT_CORE=/home/me/.npm/_npx/<hash>/node_modules/playwright-core \
      node scripts/shoot.mjs --url=http://localhost:3000/ --out=/tmp/home --beats

  Options
    --url=URL              page to open (required)
    --out=DIR              where the screenshots go (required)
    --size=WxH             viewport, default 1440x900
    --scale=N              device pixel ratio, default 1
    --beats                one screenshot per [data-beat] block, taken at the
                           end of that beat's rest
    --reduced-motion       emulate prefers-reduced-motion
    --touch                emulate a touch device, whose pointer is coarse:
                           the scene then takes its lighter path
    --no-webgl             start Chromium with 3D disabled
    --no-js                load the page with JavaScript switched off
    --ignore=REGEX         failed requests to overlook; default: none
    --expect-beats=N       fail unless the page has N [data-beat] blocks
    --expect-scene=on|off  fail unless .story has that data-scene value
    --expect-selector=CSS  fail unless something matches the selector
    --hidden=CSS           fail if anything matching the selector is displayed
    --at=X,Y               without --beats: a point on the screen, in percent
    --expect-at=CSS        with --at: fail unless what is under that point
                           matches the selector, which is how a drag on the
                           scene is checked to reach what should take it
    --block=REGEX          fail requests whose address matches, as if they
                           never arrived; they are left out of the failed-
                           request check
    --inside=CSS           with --beats: fail if anything matching the selector
                           is showing but runs off the side of the screen
    --scroll=PX            without --beats: scroll this far down before the
                           click and the screenshot
    --wait=MS              how long to let the page settle after each scroll,
                           default 2200. A jump straight to a later chapter
                           needs longer: what that chapter loads on demand
                           arrives slowly when the 3D is drawn in software
    --click=CSS            without --beats: click the first match, then fail
                           if what was being read has moved on the screen,
                           which is how switching the look is checked to keep
                           the reader's place
    --late-shaders=CHARS   fail if a shader program longer than this many
                           characters is built after the page has first
                           settled. three.js builds a program the first time
                           something is drawn with it and the page stops
                           until it is built, so the large ones should all
                           be asked for at the start
    --positions=LIST      with --beats: start,mid,end; default end
    --expect-ids=LIST      comma-separated beat IDs, in their expected order
    --expect-look=ID       fail unless the root has this data-look value
    --assert-still=MS      compare canvas screenshots after this interval
    --lose-context        lose the WebGL context and require text fallback
    --keyboard=CSS        tab to this selector and require a visible focus box
    --keyboard-at=BEAT    first scroll to this beat for the keyboard probe
    --block-late-chunks    after the opening settles, abort later JS chunks;
                           require at least one blocked chunk and a live scene
    --look-cycle=IDs       click the second look, then exercise browser Back;
